_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: It started as a side effect.
beats.note: Street Fighter II, 1991. The chained hits that built the whole genre were never designed. They fell out of a system built to do something else.

beats.text: Press a special too fast and it still came out.
beats.note: Input leniency, added so a rushed motion would not swallow your fireball. The side effect: you could cancel a normal attack straight into a special.

beats.name: Akira Nishitani
beats.role: Lead designer. On the cancel: "It didn't seem to cause any bugs, so we decided it could be a feature to expand the gameplay." They left it in, sure most players would never land it.

beats.text: "Since we decided to incorporate it, I wouldn't call it a bug."

beats.lead: The name came after the thing
beats.note: Super Street Fighter II, in 1993, added the on-screen combo counter. The mechanic itself shipped in 1991 with no name, no counter and no plan for it.

beats.line: The rule the whole genre runs on was an accident, kept on purpose.
